It makes me feel so small and disconnected. Like if I just stopped moving, stopped breathing for a second, maybe the connection would snap shut and I wouldn't have to deal with this anymore. But then I remember that stopping means nothing good happens, and the pain just keeps going.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that right now, I don't feel like I belong anywhere. My friends are there physically, or they might be online, but I feel like they're miles away because I can't even show them the real version of myself—the one who is sick, scared, and barely holding onto life. feedback_history.therapist_response: It's very hard to know if you're drowning if you're already in the water. It seems like you're feeling helpless and overwhelmed, and it's very hard to know how to get out of the panic when you can't even breathe properly.

feedback_history.patient_message:
Yeah, it is. It's the most isolating part of all this. I look at my phone and see messages from people who care about me, but reading them feels like looking at a stranger's diary. They're talking about their day, their plans, their normal lives, and it just... highlights how broken mine has become.

It makes me feel like a burden. Like if I tell them the truth—that I've had a panic attack, that I'm vomiting constantly, that I can't eat or even breathe properly—they'll either rush to "fix" me in a way that pushes me away, or they'll think I'm being dramatic again and ignore me. Either way, it feels like I'm rejecting myself by trying to connect with them.
